title: Operating-Life Enhancement of Recirculating Ball Screw Assemblies through Tribological Control and Ball-Recirculation Dynamics: A Critical Review
content: Recirculating ball screws often fail through preload loss, backlash, lubricant starvation or return-path damage long before rolling-contact fatigue, yet ISO 3408-5 rating life captures none of these modes. This review integrates ball–raceway kinematics, mixed and starved lubrication, wear–preload degradation, rolling-contact fatigue and ball-recirculation dynamics. Return-path models rarely pass impact and lubricant histories to damage models, whereas life models reduce circulation to a static loaded-ball count. Operating life is therefore formulated as a coupled competing-risk process in which fatigue, wear, return-path, thermal and functional hazards share one ball-resolved tribodynamic state. A five-level validation hierarchy, mechanism-linked life-enhancement measures and a prioritized research agenda are proposed to support physics-informed design and prognostics.
